metadata.note: The Duluth, Missabe and Iron Range ('Missabe Road') and the two companies that ran its passenger trains before it: the Duluth and Iron Range Rail Road (Duluth - Two Harbors - Tower - Ely and its Mesabi branches, 1884-1930) and the Duluth, Missabe and Northern Railway (Duluth - Wolf - Hibbing / Virginia and branches, 1893-1937). Drawn from research/branches/duluth_missabe_and_iron_range_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-06). Before this layer the map drew no DM&IR, DM&N or D&IR route. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms. Rule 4 splits, all sharing geometry: D&IR lines -> DM&N on the 10 Jan 1930 lease (the 1930 and 1932 Ely Miner ads are headed by the DM&N, so the lessee held itself out as the operator); DM&N -> DM&IR on 1 July 1937 (merger with the Spirit Lake Transfer Railway). The March 1938 conveyance of the D&IR's property to the DM&IR changes nothing operationally and is not a split. U.S. Steel's 1901 stock purchase of both roads is not a split. The last Missabe Division train ran 31 Dec 1957 (with no trains 15 May 1953 - 5 Nov 1956, drawn as a real gap); the last Iron Range Division train 15 July 1961. Freight continues under Canadian National (2004) and is not drawn. The North Shore Scenic Railroad (1990-) is drawn as tourist_rail on Duluth - Lester River only, split by operator per Rule 4.

geometry_caveats: Union Depot - Missabe Junction (about 2 mi, 46.778,-92.106 to about 46.757,-92.15) was Northern Pacific trackage used by DM&N/DM&IR trains; drawn in this company's colour on the surviving waterfront track.

Hibbing: drawn to the post-1920 station south of the Hull-Rust pit (the report's South Hibbing), ending 47.4241,-92.9478; 1901-c.1920 trains used the original Hibbing (later North Hibbing) station about 1.5 mi north, now in the pit.

Great Northern parallels: Mitchell - Hibbing (47.437,-92.915; drawn on an OHM grade within 60 m of the BNSF Hib Tac Subdivision, not on it), Wilpen - Chisholm (last 1.3 mi on the Mesabi Trail, 47.474,-92.852 to 47.483,-92.876, possibly the GN grade) and Taconite - Coleraine (2.5 mi on the Mesabi Trail, 47.300,-93.384 to 47.292,-93.424, possibly the GN grade).

Straight-line legs over 300 m: Spruce - Eveleth 2.3 mi; Mesaba junction 0.8 mi; Duluth depot throat 0.5 mi (laid along straight track); Two Harbors yard 0.4 mi; Mountain Iron junction 0.3 mi; Alborn junction 0.3 mi.

Later alignments: Mountain Iron branch on the 1960s Minntac Subdivision; Biwabik branch on the CN Iron Range Subdivision; Mesaba - Babbitt on the taconite-era branch to the Northshore pits; Union Depot is drawn as the Lake Division terminal from 1886 though it opened in 1892.
not_yet_sourced: End years that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): Iron Junction - Eveleth (DM&IR) 1951, Wolf - Virginia 1901, Biwabik Branch 1911, Western Mesaba Branch 1909, Lake Division Union Depot - Endion (DM&IR) 1951.
Start years that are the first CONFIRMED year, not the opening ([OPEN]): Wolf - Hibbing 1901 (bracket 1893-1901), Iron Junction - Eveleth 1901, Biwabik Branch 1901, Western Mesaba Branch 1895.
Single proven years ([ANCHOR]): Eveleth - Virginia 1951, Mountain Iron Branch 1901, Wilpen - Chisholm 1951 (rail vs bus not certain), Coleraine Branch 1914, Mesaba - Babbitt 1924 (low confidence).

Passenger end on every D&IR Mesabi branch and every DM&N branch: all before 1951 where the Feb 1952 Guide says freight only. Sources to try: DM&N/D&IR employee timetables, Minnesota Railroad & Warehouse Commission discontinuance orders, the Ely Miner / Virginia Enterprise / Mesaba Ore in Chronicling America.

End of the Virginia service (Nos. 11/12): between Sept 1951 and May 1953. Route of the 1901 Eveleth trains (via Spruce or via Wolf - Virginia - Rainy Junction) and of the 1951 trains into Virginia (traced 4.9 mi against about 7).

DM&N passenger start: american-rails.com says Duluth - Hibbing service began 1892, but the DM&N had no Duluth track until 22 July 1893 and no Hibbing rails until 24 Oct 1893; earliest dated evidence is the timetable effective 18 Dec 1893 (Duluth - Virginia). Conflict recorded, 1893 drawn.
Last Iron Range Division train: 15 July 1961 (american-rails.com, Wikipedia Endion station) vs 20 July 1961 (Lindahl). Same year.
D&IR -> DM&IR corporate date: conveyance March 1938 / 21 March 1938 vs mnopedia 'officially merged' July 1938. Irrelevant to drawing (the operating split is the 10 Jan 1930 lease).
Which Duluth station the Iron Range Division used year by year (Union Depot in 1951, Endion in 1961, the D&IR's own arrangements before 1892).
Whether the 1956-57 reinstated Nos. 1/2 made every stop of the 1951 schedule.
Sites not verified on the ground: the DM&N Eveleth and Virginia stations, the D&IR Tower station, Endion's original site, the 1924 Babbitt terminal.
omitted: Ely - Winton (report block 13): no confirmable passenger year; every timetable read ends at Ely, and the one web caption putting the RDC on 'Ely-Winton' is unsourced.

McKinley - Virginia (D&IR, via Gilbert) and McKinley - Sparta - Eveleth (report block 15): the Jan 1895 D&IR timetable reaches Virginia 32 min after McKinley, which fits either route; the route is unresolved, so neither is drawn.

Wales Branch, Wales - Scott Junction / Whyte (report block 17): a 1917 logging branch; the Oct 1951 Guide prints a 'WALES BRANCH' table but its times are not recoverable - could be a mixed train or a freight station list. No confirmed passenger year.
Waldo - Britton - Drummond - Rollins: FOWLER marks Rollins 'pass?'; no evidence.
Sherwood - Buhl: the 1951 Guide has a 'SHERWOOD TO BUHL' header with no recoverable times, and the adjoining table puts a bus between Wilpen and Buhl; no confirmed rail passenger year.

North Shore Scenic Railroad Lester River - Two Harbors: excursions beyond Lester River (to Palmers, Knife River, Two Harbors) ran in some seasons, but which seasons is not sourced, so only Duluth - Lester River is drawn.
Duluth - Lester Park commuter trains of the 1880s ('up to 15 daily', dropped 1892): start year not separately sourced; not drawn as a commuter_rail overlay.
A 'last passenger train' out of Ely on 19 Sept 1981: probably a farewell special before abandonment; operator and nature not established.

Freight-only lines (Rule 1): ore spurs and mine leads, the Proctor yard and dock tracks, the Interstate and Spirit Lake Transfer terminal roads, and the whole system after 1961 except the 1990+ tourist operation.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap, 16.4 mi against the documented 18.1 mi Allen Junction - McKinley (FOWLER; american-rails.com '18-mile extension to McKinley via Wyman'). Allen Junction - Biwabik on CN Iron Range Subdivision / Hinsdale Spur / Duluth Missabe & Iron Range Ry ways; Biwabik - McKinley (about 3 mi) on unnamed abandoned grade, ending at 47.5101,-92.4085. No straight-line leg longer than 300 m. Parallels the DM&N's Biwabik branch closely at Biwabik; the trace stayed on the D&IR-side ways. segments.note: The D&IR's Mesabi Range line. Both ends are withheld unknowns. 1895 is the first CONFIRMED year, not the opening (built 1890 [MC] / 1892 [AR]): the D&IR timetable in effect 23 Jan 1895 runs Duluth - Allen Junction 6:00 - Biwabik 6:40 - McKinley 6:58 - Virginia 7:30 PM [VE95]. 1909 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: FOWLER tags Colby '1909t' (a 1909 public timetable). By Sept 1951 Allen Junction - Eveleth was 'Freight Service only' [OG51] - do NOT draw it to 1951. If service outlived the 1930 lease it would be DM&N-run, but nothing establishes that. Do not extend either end without evidence. Headway is an estimate from the one or two daily trains the cited timetables show and is NOT sourced for every year.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap plus OpenHistoricalMap, 13.9 mi against the documented 15.6 mi Mesaba - Babbitt (FOWLER). Drawn on the DM&IR branch east from Mesaba (a way named Duluth Missabe & Iron Range Ry) to its end at 47.5984,-91.8769. APPROXIMATED: the first 0.8 mi joins the branch to the Vermilion line at Mesaba with a straight line (47.5694,-92.1325 to 47.5766,-92.1186). BABBITT STATION: the 1924 terminal was the Mesabi Iron Company's original Babbitt, not the present city of Babbitt (founded in the 1950s, about 8 mi north); its site was not verified, and the line is drawn to the east end of the surviving DM&IR branch, near the Northshore Mining (ex-Reserve) pits. LATER ALIGNMENT: the surviving branch was rebuilt for the taconite era and may not follow the D&IR's 1920s grade.

segments.note: Single proven year [ANCHOR], low confidence: FOWLER lists 'Babbitt 1924TG(tm)' - Babbitt shown as the terminus of a service in the 1924 Time Saver Guide, a public passenger guide. The Babbitt mine (Mesabi Iron Co.) was the first taconite plant, 1922-24. Possibly a mixed train; not established. FOWLER also notes 'irregular service (passenger?) to Dunka' in the 1914 Guide. The 1951 Guide has a 'MESABA TO BABBITT' table header but no recoverable times, which neither confirms nor denies 1951 service. Service may well have run wider, but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. Headway is a placeholder estimate.

segments.note: Tourist excursions on the ex-D&IR lakefront line from the Duluth Depot (the former Union Depot). The North Shore Scenic Railroad 'began operating in 1990' [Wikipedia], run by Donald Shank in 1990 and the Goldfine family 1991-1996; the Lake Superior Railroad Museum took over in 1996. The two private operators share this feature and colour under one brand name. Only the short Duluth - Lester River run is drawn: which seasons ran through to Knife River or Two Harbors is NOT established. Excursions are seasonal (May - December); the headway is an estimate.
